title: Size a course in minutes, not points
statement: Size a course's length in measured minutes for each kind of activity, never by holding points constant, since equal points can take very different times.
example: On one platform, nearly identical points, about 25,200, took 3.0 times the minutes in a comprehension course as in a fluency course.
detail: A second-grade redesign claimed to be duration-neutral because its total points stayed fixed. A feasibility red team queried the platform's activity data: a fluency course and a comprehension course with essentially identical points, 25,250 and 25,213, took 23,051 and 69,860 minutes, 0.913 against 2.771 minutes per point, 3.0 times the time (`grade3-reading/ti-courseplans/courses/g2-reading/analysis/redteam-3-feasibility.md`, lines 67-74). The narrowed rebuild that followed recorded comprehension work at 2.87 minutes per point against 0.92 for fluency and kept the duration-neutral claim only for a one-for-one swap of items (`grade3-reading/ti-courseplans/courses/g2-reading/analysis/optionB-prime-narrow-rebuild.md`, lines 18 and 38-39).
against: Minutes per point also reflect how the platform's points are configured, not only how long the work takes (`grade3-reading/ti-courseplans/courses/g2-reading/analysis/redteam-3-feasibility.md`, line 100).

evidence.quote: The first two rows are a near-natural experiment: **essentially identical XP (25,250 vs 25,213), 3.0x the minutes.**
Alpha Read comprehension = **2.87 min/XP** vs fluency 0.92 — ~3× slower → real bloat.
This is the one scope where "duration-neutral" is actually true.
Caveat in the plan's favor: min/XP also reflects XP-economy *configuration*, not only intrinsic task speed.
